'''Valerie Sheares Ashby''' is an American chemist and university professor who currently serves as president of the [[University of Maryland, Baltimore County]].<ref>{{cite web |title=About Our President |url=https://president.umbc.edu/about-our-president/ |website=UMBC Office of the President |publisher=University of Maryland, Baltimore County |access-date=22 October 2022}}</ref> She was the Dean of [[Trinity College of Arts and Sciences]] at [[Duke University]]<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=Valerie S Ashby {{!}} Scholars@Duke|url=https://scholars.duke.edu/person/valerie.ashby|access-date=2021-05-31|website=scholars.duke.edu|language=en|archive-date=2022-04-04|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220404144241/https://scholars.duke.edu/person/valerie.ashby|url-status=dead}}</ref> from 2015 to 2022 and formerly chair of the chemistry department at the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]] from 2012 to 2015. With her research group, she holds ten patents.<ref name="endeavors">{{Cite journal|last=Jacobs|first=Danielle|date=2007|title=Unbroken Bonds|url=https://admin.trinity.duke.edu/dean/valerie-sheares-ashby|journal=Endeavors|language=EN}}</ref> On April 4, 2022, it was announced<ref>{{cite web |url=https://news.umbc.edu/valerie-sheares-ashby-named-next-president-of-umbc/|title=Valerie Sheares Ashby Named Next President of UMBC, Arriving from Duke in August 2022 – UMBC: University of Maryland, Baltimore County |date=4 April 2022 }}</ref> that Ashby would assume the position of president of the [[University of Maryland, Baltimore County]].

==Early life and education==
Ashby was born and grew up in [[Clayton, North Carolina]]. She was first introduced to science through her father, who was a high school math and science teacher.<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal|last=Wafle|first=Nick|date=2002-08-26|title=Women in Chemistry: Chemist, Teacher, Scholar, Mentor|url=http://pubs.acs.org/cen/women/8034/print/8034sci2.html|journal=Chemical & Engineering News|language=EN|volume=80|issue=34|pages=34|doi=10.1021/cen-v080n034.p034|issn=0009-2347|url-access=subscription}}</ref> Ashby was graduated from the [[University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill]] (UNC) with a B.A. in chemistry in 1988.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2015-05-16|title=UNC Chemistry Valerie Ashby|url=http://www.chem.unc.edu/people/faculty/ashby|access-date=2021-05-31|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150516223428/http://www.chem.unc.edu/people/faculty/ashby|archive-date=2015-05-16}}</ref> After her graduation, she worked as an agricultural and organic chemist at [[Rhône-Poulenc]], located in the nearby [[Research Triangle Park]].<ref name=":1" />

=== Graduate studies ===
Ashby returned to UNC for graduate studies in 1989, working as a research assistant in the lab of Prof. [[Joseph M. DeSimone|Joseph DeSimone]] and completing her thesis, entitled ''Synthesis and Characterization of [[Thiophene]]-Based [[Polyaryletherketone|Poly(Arylene Ether Ketones)]] and [[Polysulfone|Poly(Arylene Ether Sulfones)]]'', in 1994. During her graduate studies, Ashby worked as a visiting scientist at [[IBM]]'s [[Almaden Research Center]] in [[San Jose, California]], in the summer of 1992, where she worked on the synthesis of [[thiophene]]-containing [[polyetherimide]]s.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Valerie Ashby CV|url=https://trinity.duke.edu/sites/trinity.duke.edu/files/documents/Valerie_Ashby_6_15_CV.pdf|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210531190038/https://trinity.duke.edu/sites/trinity.duke.edu/files/documents/Valerie_Ashby_6_15_CV.pdf|archive-date=2021-05-31}}</ref> She also spent the summer of 1993 as a visiting scientist at the [[Eastman Chemical Company]] in [[Kingsport, Tennessee]], where she examined the role of catalysts in the color body origin in poly(ester amide)s.<ref name=":0" />

=== Postdoctoral studies ===
After graduating with her Ph.D., Ashby worked as a [[National Science Foundation|NSF]] and [[NATO]] Postdoctoral Fellow at the [[Johannes Gutenberg University of Mainz]]'s Institute for Organic Chemistry in [[Germany]]. At Mainz, Ashby worked under the direction of Prof. Reimund Stadler on the synthesis of [[Block copolymers|ABC block copolymers]].<ref name=":2" />

==Career==
=== Iowa State University ===
Ashby began her independent academic career at [[Iowa State University]] as an assistant professor in 1996, and was promoted to associate professor in 2002.<ref name=":1" /> While at Iowa State, Ashby was a mentor for the Iowa State University Program for Women in Science & Engineering, a summer research program for undergraduate and high school students.{{citation needed|date=March 2024}}

=== University of North Carolina – Chapel Hill ===
Ashby spent August 2003 to June 2004 on sabbatical leave at the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] under the direction of Prof. [[Robert Langer]]. In August 2003, Ashby also began her appointment as associate professor at UNC Chapel Hill.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://endeavors.unc.edu/win2007/ashby.php|title=Unbroken Bonds {{!}} endeavors|website=endeavors.unc.edu|language=en|access-date=2017-04-12}}</ref> In 2005, Ashby was awarded an NSF grant<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=0450099|title=NSF Award Search: Award#0450099 – AGEP Collaborative Research Training: North Carolina Alliance to Create Opportunity Through Education|website=www.nsf.gov|access-date=2017-04-12}}</ref> that aimed to increase the number of underrepresented minorities receiving doctoral degrees in STEM fields. Her work helped to increase the Ph.D. completion rate for underrepresented minorities from about 60% to 85% at UNC.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.timeshighereducation.com/news/spot-black-talent-sooner-boost-academic-diversity-says-dean#survey-answer|title=Spot black talent sooner to boost academic diversity, says dean|date=2017-03-02|work=Times Higher Education (THE)|access-date=2017-04-12|language=en}}</ref> She was appointed Vice Chair of Undergraduate Studies in August 2005. Ashby was granted the rank of full professor and the Bowman and Gordon Gray Distinguished Term Professor of Chemistry in July 2007. In July 2012 she was named chair of the department of chemistry and the faculty director of the UNC Chapel Hill Graduate School Initiative for Minority Excellence (IME) in July 2014.{{citation needed|date=March 2024}}

Through her career, Ashby has accumulated numerous awards, including the National Science Foundation Career Development Award, the DuPont Young Faculty Award, the 3M Young Faculty Award, the UNC Chapel Hill General Alumni Association Faculty Service Award, the J. Carlyle Sitterson Freshman Teaching Award, the UNC Student Undergraduate Teaching Award, and the Johnston Teaching Award for Undergraduate Teaching.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://admin.trinity.duke.edu/dean/ashby/press-kit|title=Valerie Sheares Ashby {{!}} Trinity Administration|website=admin.trinity.duke.edu|language=en|access-date=2017-04-12}}</ref>

===Duke University===
On May 7, 2015, [[Duke University]] President [[Richard H. Brodhead]] and Provost [[Sally Kornbluth]] announced that Ashby would be the next dean of [[Trinity College of Arts & Sciences]] at [[Duke University]] succeeding [[Laurie L. Patton|Laurie Patton]], who became the new president of [[Middlebury College|Middlebury]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://today.duke.edu/2015/05/ashby-final|title=Valerie Ashby to Become Arts & Sciences Dean|work=Duke Today|date=13 May 2015 }}</ref> The search committee that nominated and unanimously supported Ashby consisted of faculty members, students, administrators and trustees.

===University of Maryland, Baltimore County===
[[File:UMBC-Pres-Inaug-79.jpg|thumb|Ashby being sworn in as UMBC president, 2023]]
On Monday, April 4, 2022, outgoing [[UMBC]] President [[Freeman Hrabowski]] announced that Ashby would be the next President of UMBC, effective August 1, 2022.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://president.umbc.edu/valerie-sheares-ashby-named-next-president-of-umbc/|title=Valerie Sheares Ashby Named Next President of UMBC|work=UMBC Office of the President|access-date=2022-04-04}}</ref> Ashby also holds a faculty appointment in UMBC's Department of Chemistry and Biochemistry.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Valerie Sheares Ashby {{!}} College Excellence Program |url=https://highered.aspeninstitute.org/profile/valerie-sheares-ashby |access-date=2025-09-15 |website=highered.aspeninstitute.org |language=en}}</ref>
